methodological_questions: Does adherence to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predict winning after controlling for team quality?
Is a 54-series sample powered for a series-level test?
Can the recommended mix be derived without leakage or outcome-derived labels?
Are play-type labels and suppression measures reliable enough?

historical_evidence.finding: Series-level AVOID share vs winning: game-level rho=-0.19 p=0.008 (inflated n, team-quality confound); series-level rho=-0.26 p=0.07 at n=50, underpowered (~80 series stated as needed for p<0.05); still confounded by team quality (verdict recorded as inconclusive).

pct_ran_BEST minus pct_ran_AVOID vs series wins with a talent control: talent_diff_z +0.737 p=0.0213; adapt_diff_z +0.328 p=0.2755 (cluster p=0.2449); univariate adapt beta=+0.311 p=0.1128; n~55 series cannot separate adaptation from roster quality.

Holdout games with a mix closer to the model's recommended mix scored higher: raw gap +5.18 ORtg, strength-controlled +3.27 ORtg; n=908 game-team rows; no CI stated; same-pipeline validation. Model regret is non-negative by construction.

System BEST vs constrained league mix: headline gap +0.269 PPP is CUT-driven; non-CUT BEST vs mix gap +0.010 (p=0.1709, n=136); L3 matchup non-CUT gap +0.001 (p=0.3277, n=47); recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null). BEST vs AVOID gap +0.692 (n=169).
DRIVE-as-BEST counter vs constrained mix: observed gap -0.066 vs fixed baseline (p=0.2175), n=44, MDE 0.180 PPP at 80% power; cannot distinguish a null from effects up to 0.18 PPP.
Playoff adaptation pivots: 10/12 pairs within 0.10 PPP of non-pivot; two pairs PIVOT_LOSES (pivot worse than staying); recorded as powered null across 74 matchups.
Counter ranking is not stable across population, team and matchup levels; small cells (n_mu 5 to 696); mechanical floor risk recorded.
Suppressor rankings mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control.
Only 2/30 stars had a stable top suppressor across seasons (75% rule); recorded as null.
Sequential suppression results with no multiplicity correction and small n_after cells (32-95).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Series-level test of recommended-mix (AVOID share) adherence vs winning
failed_approaches.why: n=50 series underpowered (~80 needed); team-quality confound unresolved.

failed_approaches.what_failed: BEST-minus-AVOID adherence predicting series wins after controlling for net-rating talent
failed_approaches.why: Adaptation term non-significant after talent control; n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matchup-specific non-CUT BEST beating a feasibility-weighted league mix
failed_approaches.why: Powered null; headline gap CUT-driven; regression-to-the-mean/selection and small sample limitations recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: DRIVE-as-BEST counter beating a constrained baseline
failed_approaches.why: n=44, MDE 0.18 PPP, too coarse to detect plausible effects.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pivoting to a listed counter sustaining higher PPP in the playoffs
failed_approaches.why: Powered null; some pivots were worse than staying.

evidence_establishes: Earlier series-level tests of essentially this question (FAM:SF-CHT-039, FAM:SF-APPS-027) at n=50-55 were recorded as untestable/inconclusive: the adherence-to-win association was not distinguishable from team quality.
A game-level alignment-to-efficiency association was recorded as supported (FAM:SF-APPM-001) with strength control, but via same-pipeline validation and with no CI.
The headline BEST advantage is driven by CUT, and non-CUT, matchup-specific recommendations showed no gain over a constrained league mix (FAM:SF-APPS-023, recorded as a powered null).
Recommendations (counter rankings, top suppressors) are unstable across levels and seasons (FAM:SF-APPM-055, FAM:SF-APPA-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether adherence predicts series wins independent of team quality at adequate power: no returned record answers this.
Whether any adherence effect holds out-of-sample on the 2025-26 data with a mix fixed in advance.
Whether the game-level alignment effect (FAM:SF-APPM-001) reflects causal benefit rather than the model's by-construction relationship to efficiency or to team strength.
Whether the 54-series sample here is a superset of or overlaps the earlier n=50/55 samples (not stated in the records).
own_inferences: Because 54 series is nearly identical to the n=50-55 already tried, adding at most a few series will not change power; the series-level test will likely return another inconclusive result.
A game-level test with series-clustered errors and a team-quality control is the only design with enough observations, but effective information is still bounded by about 54 clusters.

If the recommended mix is derived from the same games used to score adherence, a positive association would be partly mechanical, which makes the game-level supported result of FAM:SF-APPM-001 weak support.
CUT dominance suggests adherence may largely proxy for rim-pressure/efficient-play-type frequency that is also correlated with team quality.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'suppression-conditional recommended mix' and how it is trained is not given in the task statement.
Whether the 2025-26 playoffs (complete only from 2026-06-21) are included, since the question was posed on 2026-06-16; the 54-series count may change.
Reliability of the derived play-type labels is not documented in the retrieved records.
I did not read the full records (several were truncated), so details of the controls and sample overlap are missing.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history this would look like a straightforward proceed. The records show nearly the same series-level test failed twice (n=50, n=55) for power and talent confounding, and a powered null for non-CUT recommendations, so the decision moves to proceed only with changes: a pre-specified, leakage-free, talent-controlled design with a lower expectation of a decisive answer.

blocking_constraints.text: 54 series is about the same as the 50-55 already recorded as underpowered; ~80 series were estimated as needed even for a marginal univariate effect, and a talent-adjusted effect needs more.
Team quality drives both adherence and winning; the earlier talent control left adaptation p=0.275, and a 54-series sample cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.

prior_work.summary: Series-level versions were recorded as untestable/inconclusive (n=50, 55). A game-level alignment effect was supported with same-pipeline validation. Non-CUT matchup-specific recommendations showed a powered null against a league mix. The question as posed (series-level winning) is not answered.

risks.text: About 54 series; an odds-ratio-level effect after talent adjustment is undetectable at conventional power.
Team quality, opponent strength, game state and score effects drive both play-type mix and winning.

If the recommended mix or suppression labels are fit on games that also provide adherence or outcomes, adherence will mechanically predict efficiency and wins; the mix must be frozen from earlier data.
BEST/AVOID labels are defined from PPP outcomes, so adherence is partly outcome-defined; model regret is non-negative by construction (FAM:SF-APPM-001).
BEST counters selected for high PPP in small cells will regress; recorded as a limitation in FAM:SF-APPS-023.
Counter rankings and feasibility constraints produce mechanical baselines and small-cell artifacts (FAM:SF-APPM-055).
Top suppressors and best counters are unstable across seasons (2/30 stable), so the recommendation itself is noisy.
Play-type tendencies and league style shift across seasons, so a mix trained on 2022-25 may not transfer to 2025-26.
Many play types, suppression conditions and cut variants invite forking paths; earlier records lacked correction.
Play-type labels are derived from play-by-play and may be misclassified; CUT/OTHER artifacts were flagged earlier.

design.estimand: Within-season change in a team's single-game win probability, and its series win probability, per 1 SD increase in adherence (L1-distance-based closeness to a recommended mix frozen before the evaluated games), adjusted for pre-game team strength, opponent strength, home court, and opponent suppression exposure.
design.unit: Primary: team-game (clustered by series and team-season). Secondary and descriptive only: the series (~54), with no confirmatory claim.
design.sample: Fit the recommended mix and suppression definitions on 2022-23 to 2024-25 only. Evaluate on 2025-26 regular season and playoffs once complete (playoffs from 2026-06-21), plus a rolling-origin check where each season is predicted from earlier seasons. Exclude CUT-only adherence from the primary measure and report CUT-inclusive as a sensitivity analysis.
design.power: Series-level: 54 series is ~50-55 already recorded as underpowered (~80 needed even unadjusted); a detectable effect after talent adjustment is likely large (OR>~2 per SD). Before data access, run a simulation-based power analysis with the observed adherence SD and talent-adherence correlation (~0.12); if the MDE exceeds a plausible effect, report as untestable rather than run a confirmatory test. Game-level: report the effective sample size after clustering.
design.controls: Pre-game net rating or point-differential-based strength (computed from earlier games only), opponent strength, home court, rest, game-state exposure (score/time), and playoff round; team fixed effects in a within-team specification; negative-control adherence computed against a randomly permuted opponent suppression condition.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: adherence to a mix recommended for a different, unmatched opponent should predict winning as well as the true conditional mix if the effect is generic team style, which would refute the suppression-conditional claim. (2) Permutation of the opponent label within season. (3) Adherence measured from the same games used to train the mix must be shown to be inflated relative to the frozen-mix version. (4) Predicting outcomes before the next game, not post hoc.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary test (game-level, frozen mix, non-CUT, talent-adjusted, clustered SE). All other cuts (per play type, per suppressor, per round) are exploratory, and Holm-adjusted if reported.
design.decision_rule: Supported if the primary coefficient is in the predicted direction with a clustered 95% CI excluding zero and it survives the placebo and the frozen-mix leakage check. Rejected only if the 95% CI lies within a pre-set equivalence margin. Otherwise report inconclusive/untestable; do not claim series-level support from 54 series.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files and derived play-type records as of 2026-06-16 for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season; 2025-26 playoff evaluation frozen after 2026-06-21 completion. Record the extraction hash, graph-database build version and the frozen-mix training cutoff.

methodological_questions: Does adherence to a recommended play-type mix conditional on opponent suppression predict game or series wins?
How is the recommended mix derived without leakage or outcome-derived labels?
Is 54 series sufficient power for a series-level test?
How reliable are play-type possession labels and suppression measures, and how do confounders such as team quality affect the association?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-16, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
Adhering to a suppression-conditional recommended mix predicts winning.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 54 series

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
